avtandil.overview: Tinatin sends Arabia’s commander to find Tariel. Their sworn friendship leads him to seek Nestan and help rescue her from Kadjeti before returning to marry Tinatin.
insights: Friendship widens his romantic quest; his coercion and killings complicate his resourcefulness.

tariel.overview: India’s commander loves Nestan-Darejan, kills her intended bridegroom, and searches for her in exile. With Avtandil and Pridon, he rescues her from Kadjeti.
insights: The panther skin embodies his grief and love. Friendship turns his suffering into action.
tariel.role: Commander of India; knight in the panther’s skin

nestan.overview: India’s heir pledges herself to Tariel and directs the bridegroom’s killing. After Davar sends her away, she escapes one court and sends letters from Kadjeti.
insights: Her plans and letters preserve her agency while imprisonment limits her freedom.
nestan.role: Princess and heir of India; Tariel’s beloved

tinatin.overview: Crowned sovereign by Rostevan, Tinatin sends Avtandil to find the stranger and supports his promise to Tariel. She marries Avtandil and forms a sisterhood with Nestan.
insights: Her command begins the search; her support lets love and friendship coexist.

asmat.overview: Asmat carries the lovers’ messages, stays with Tariel in exile, and introduces Avtandil to him. On their return, Tariel grants her one seventh of India.
insights: Her care sustains friendship; her resistance to threats shows the limits of coercion.

pridon.overview: Tariel helps the wounded king of Mulghazanzar defeat his cousins. Pridon shares news of Nestan, aids the rescue at Kadjeti, and hosts the lovers’ wedding.
insights: His care, hospitality and knowledge of routes make cooperation more than shared strength.
pridon.role: King of Mulghazanzar; sworn brother of the knights

fatman.overview: Fatman shelters Nestan and equips her escape from Gulansharo. Later she welcomes Avtandil, discovers Nestan’s whereabouts, and sends a messenger into Kadjeti.
insights: Her hospitality turns private protection into a network of information and communication.
fatman.role: Gulansharo hostess and protector of Nestan

rostevan.overview: Rostevan crowns Tinatin and teaches her generosity. Loving Avtandil as a foster-son, he resists his departure, then welcomes his return and approves the marriage.
insights: Paternal love and royal command pull him in different directions before reconciliation.

shermadin.overview: Shermadin guards Avtandil’s household, troops and frontier during his absence. He announces his return and later delivers his testament after the secret departure.
insights: His dependable service and willingness to stay behind make the visible adventures possible.

sograt.overview: The elderly vizier jokes with Rostevan and intercedes for Avtandil despite fearing royal anger. He later reports the knight’s secret departure.
insights: His humor allows candor, while mediation exposes him to the costs of another person’s promises.
sograt.role: Elderly vizier of the Arabian court

parsadan.overview: Parsadan raises Tariel with the queen, then arranges Nestan’s foreign marriage. After Tariel kills the prince, he threatens Davar; he dies before the lovers return.
insights: His marriage plans pit paternal authority against the lovers’ pledges and Tariel’s inheritance claim.

queen_india.overview: The queen raises Tariel and helps arrange Nestan’s marriage. After Parsadan’s death, she receives the returning lovers, enthrones them, gives gifts, and pardons Ramaz.
insights: Her shift from mourning to generosity makes the restored royal household publicly visible.

saridan.overview: Saridan, Tariel’s father, brings India’s seventh kingdom into Parsadan’s service and becomes Amirbar. After his death and a year’s mourning, Tariel receives his command.
insights: His alliance roots Tariel’s inheritance claim in both royal descent and service to Parsadan.

davari.overview: Parsadan’s sister educates Nestan. Threatened with death after the bridegroom’s killing, she beats Nestan, orders her removal toward the sea, and kills herself.
insights: Fear explains her retaliation without excusing her violence against the woman in her care.

khvarazmsha.overview: The King of Khwarazm’s son comes to India to marry Nestan and inherit the throne. Before the wedding, Tariel enters his tent and kills him.
insights: His limited voice and sudden death expose the human cost of the opposed political marriage.
khvarazmsha.role: Foreign prince chosen as Nestan’s bridegroom

khvarazmshah.overview: The King of Khwarazm welcomes the Indian sovereigns’ proposal that his son marry Nestan. The prince travels to India, where Tariel kills him before the wedding.
insights: His response frames the wedding as an agreement between ruling houses rather than the lovers’ choice.
khvarazmshah.role: Ruler of Khwarazm; father of the proposed bridegroom

ramaz.overview: Ramaz conceals an ambush behind his welcome. Tariel defeats him and Parsadan pardons him under tribute. After attacking India again, he receives another pardon.
insights: Repeated conflict tests the relationship between military power, submission and mercy.

usen.overview: Gulansharo’s chief merchant and Fatman’s husband promises to hide Nestan. Drunk at court, he reveals her presence and offers her as a bride for the Sea King’s son.
insights: Courtly ambition and a broken oath endanger the woman protected within his household.

usam.overview: Usam leads the merchant caravan Avtandil meets at the seashore. After the knight defeats their pirate attackers, he speaks for the grateful merchants.
insights: He gives the threatened merchants a voice and acknowledges the obligations created by rescue.

chashnagiri.overview: Finding Fatman with Avtandil, the court favorite threatens to expose her part in Nestan’s escape. At Fatman’s request, Avtandil secretly kills him.
insights: His access to court turns an intimate confidence into a threat against an entire household.

surkhavi.overview: The Sea King confines Nestan as a bride for his absent son. After her rescue, he welcomes the companions, accepts conquered Kadjeti, and supplies their onward ship.
insights: His generous welcome after the rescue complicates his earlier control over Nestan’s marriage.

dulardukht.overview: Kadjeti’s ruler raises Rosan and Rodia and chooses captive Nestan for Rosan. She leaves to mourn her sister, taking the sorcerers but leaving warriors on guard.
insights: Her dynastic plans impose captivity; her absence opens a way into the guarded fortress.
dulardukht.role: Ruler of Kadjeti and guardian of its young princes

rosan.overview: Rosan is one of the dead Kadji king’s young sons, raised by Dulardukht with Rodia. His aunt chooses captive Nestan as his bride and postpones the wedding.
insights: His proposed marriage makes a captive woman’s future part of the ruling family’s plans.

rodia.overview: Rodia and Rosan are the dead Kadji king’s young sons. Their aunt Dulardukht raises them while ruling Kadjeti; Rodia receives no separate speech or action.
insights: His brief mention establishes family responsibilities without Rosan’s separate marriage role.

roshak.overview: Roshak leads a hundred Kadji raiders who intercept Nestan after her escape. Recognizing her as a woman, he takes her toward Kadjeti as a gift for Dulardukht.
insights: His decision turns a chance encounter into another act of political captivity.

eldest_hunting_brother.overview: The eldest brother wants to seize the unknown Tariel. After the youngest is wounded, he helps carry him away and gives Avtandil the lead he needs.
insights: Competitive pride ends in costly defeat, yet the brothers’ testimony advances the search.
eldest_hunting_brother.role: Unnamed hunter from the Khataeti region

middle_hunting_brother.overview: The middle brother wants Tariel’s horse during the hunters’ challenge. After the youngest is wounded, he helps bring him away and tells Avtandil where Tariel went.
insights: His desire for the horse reveals how the hunters treat an unknown traveler as a possession.
middle_hunting_brother.role: Unnamed hunter from the Khataeti region

youngest_hunting_brother.overview: The youngest hunter tries to stop Tariel after his brothers permit the challenge. Tariel’s whip splits his head; his brothers carry him away unconscious.
insights: His defeat establishes the danger of force before Avtandil chooses a more cautious approach.
youngest_hunting_brother.role: Unnamed hunter from the Khataeti region

khatavian_informant.overview: A Khatavian envoy secretly warns Tariel that Ramaz’s welcome hides an ambush. Remembering Saridan’s care, he repays that debt and changes Tariel’s preparations.
insights: Past care crosses political lines: a personal debt interrupts a ruler’s deception.

tariel_surgeon.overview: When Tariel meets the wounded Pridon, an attendant extracts the arrowheads and binds his injuries. Pridon then tells the story of his cousins’ attack.
insights: The friendship begins with skilled care as well as martial respect.

usen_gardener.overview: Usen’s gardener meets Avtandil at the landing, explains Gulansharo’s trade customs, and runs to Fatman with news of the traveler while Usen is absent.
insights: His practical knowledge opens the city’s commercial and social networks to Avtandil.

fatman_messenger.overview: Fatman’s enslaved sorcerer travels unseen into Kadjeti. He delivers her letter, reassures Nestan of its source, and returns with her replies and token.
insights: Nestan verifies the message before replying; trustworthy communication makes the rescue possible.

kadji_informant.overview: A retainer from Roshak’s raiding party recounts Nestan’s capture. Fatman overhears him, asks him to repeat the story, and learns where to direct her search.
insights: A captor’s casual story becomes information that can be used against the captors.

sea_kings_son.overview: The Sea King’s son is away at war when his father chooses Nestan as his bride. She escapes before the marriage; no meeting or conversation between them is narrated.
insights: His absence leaves others deciding the marriage while Nestan acts to escape it.

rustaveli.overview: Rustaveli introduces the heroes, praises Tamar, and reflects on poetry and love. The self-named poetic voice frames their adventures rather than joining them.
insights: His invitation to share Tariel’s sorrow frames heroic suffering through sympathy.
